messages:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — I sketched a lightweight PRD for the next quarter's serving runtime changes: kernel selector pluggability, an attention micro-optimizations RFC, and a tightened KV cache policy. Need to align on scope and launch gates. TL;DR: ship something safe for Dedicated customers first, experimental on Hosted.
Maya Patel: Sounds good. Can you paste the acceptance criteria here? we should be concrete for launch decisions.
Alex Chen: Sure — rough draft inline: 
```
Acceptance criteria (v0):
- Kernel selector supports at least 2 kernel families selectable per model.
- No customer-visible latency regression > 10% P95 compared to baseline for "common seq lengths".
- KV cache TTLs configurable per route; default eviction must not increase tail latency > 5ms.
- Canary rollout path + automatic fallback to previous kernel on >5% error spike.
```
Jamal Ortiz: Question: how are we measuring "common seq lengths"? need a concrete set (e.g., 16, 64, 512). also define baseline (current quantized runtime at Canary cluster)
Sasha Levin: +1 to Jamal. Also add functional correctness checks for quantized kernels (bit-exactness not required, but top-1/3 generation quality delta < 1% on eval suite)
Kai Wong: For KV cache policy — are we doing per-tenant isolation? I worry about cache poisoning and cross-tenant leaks if we change retention behavior.
Alex Chen: Good call. Add to acceptance: per-tenant namespace enforced; cache keys must be namespaced and encrypted at rest. Edge-case: if customers pin model variants, selector must not swap kernel family across pinned variant.
Olivia Park: From product side I need launch gating items: audit logs for kernel switches, rollbacks within 2 minutes, and cost delta estimate < 10% for Dedicated plans. Without logs we can't sign off enterprise compliance.
Maya Patel: Ops checklist: deploy plan, canary % progression (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%), automated circuit-breaker on error/slo violations, and run a 24h soak at 25% before ramp to prod
Alex Chen: Edge cases to call out in PRD/RFC: mixed-batch with different kernel families (compat matrix), extremely long seqs that overflow KV cache, and models with custom CUDA ops that the selector can't use — must fallback gracefully.
Jamal Ortiz: Proposed mitigation for mixed-batch: add a batching policy that buckets by kernel capability; if mismatched, either split the batch or run fallback kernel. We should include measurable perf impact estimates for both.
Sasha Levin: UX for engineers: add a runtime flag `--kernel-preference=latency|throughput|compat` and per-route annotations in config. Example snippet: `route.annotations.kernel_preference=latency`.
InfraBot: deploy:canary started — cluster=eu-west-1-canary, id=deploy-2361234500, target=1% traffic
Olivia Park: Action items: Alex to update PRD with seq-length buckets and acceptance thresholds; Jamal to draft fallback behavior and perf numbers; Sasha to add route annotation RFC; Maya to own the rollout playbook. Deadline: EOD Wed.
Alex Chen: Thanks team — I'll open PRD in GH and link here. If anyone has burning concerns about scope, flag now. Otherwise we'll iterate there and convene a short RFC review Thurs 10am.
